best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Competitors Mobilize Federal Lobbying on Access
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a multi-sided marketplace connecting patients to providers across telehealth and in-person care, creating direct exposure to anti-kickback enforcement and state medical advertising rules that govern referral economics. Four competing telehealth platforms filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth access and reimbursement topics in the past 60 days, signaling coordinated industry positioning ahead of potential HHS or state legislative activity. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include fee-splitting scrutiny under state medical practice acts and consumer protection claims tied to provider verification standards. The NY, CA, and TX markets represent material exposure given their top-three state status and active medical board enforcement postures.
best_narrative.cold_first_touch_frame:
Subject: Competitors' Federal Telehealth Lobbying + NY Advertising Risk Dear Public Policy Head, Four of your primary competitors just filed federal telehealth lobbying disclosures within the past two months, signaling coordinated positioning on access and reimbursement policy. Given Zocdoc's marketplace model and exposure to anti-kickback law and state medical advertising rules, understanding the lobbying agenda before regulatory bodies respond is critical for your government affairs team's positioning. Would a 15-minute call on Thursday work to map the immediate state and federal pressure points? Best,
[Rep Name]
best_narrative.worked_deal_revival_frame: BDR: Your competitors filed federal telehealth lobbying disclosures two months ago, and we're seeing NY medical board guidance shifts on marketplace referral practices. This timing creates an opening to refresh your government affairs team's intelligence before the next enforcement wave hits. Prospect: We're tracking this internally, but the landscape is moving fast. BDR Pivot: Exactly. A 10-minute sync with your compliance leadership would let us show how your peers are structuring their state advocacy response and where NY's enforcement priorities are landing this quarter.

best_narrative.headline: Spring Health: Competitors File Federal Telehealth Lobbying Push
best_narrative.body: Spring Health operates as a pure-play mental health platform with state behavioral health licensing exposure across NY, CA, and FL, creating material risk if regulatory standards shift faster than industry coordination occurs. Two direct competitors filed federal telehealth lobbying disclosures in April 2026, signaling an acceleration in industry advocacy around scope-of-practice, licensure reciprocity, and reimbursement policy. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for enterprise mental health operators include state-by-state behavioral health board action on asynchronous prescribing oversight and employer-plan contract terms tied to licensed provider density. The window to align your government affairs team with peer positioning and federal strategy conversations narrows as filing velocity increases.
